text:
Confused flour beetle (Tribolium confusum) -- similar in appearance and habits to the red flour beetle, differing mainly in antennae shape and other minor features.

Description and damage: the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (2005) describes T. confusum as a widespread pest that, like the red flour beetle, feeds primarily on grain dust and broken/damaged kernels rather than sound whole grain. It multiplies rapidly in poorly cleaned storage facilities and contributes to secondary quality degradation and contamination of stored grain.
